citation: Attendance — National Network of Partnership Schools (NNPS). (2001). https://www.nnps.jhucsos.com
title: One-Year Action Plan for Partnerships linking engagement activities to school improvement goals
description: A reusable yearly planning structure in which a school's Action Team for Partnerships writes a One-Year Action Plan that selects and schedules family and community engagement activities across the school year. The activities "must be connected to goals for a welcoming climate and for student success that are included in the School Improvement Plan." The plan focuses on two academic goals, one behavioral goal and one overall goal for a welcoming school climate, and the team evaluates the quality of each activity implemented to continually improve outreach to all families.
requirements: Goals in the Action Plan must be connected to goals already included in the School Improvement Plan.
An Action Team for Partnerships must be assembled to write and carry out the plan.
constraints: The plan covers one school year and is assessed for quality and progress at year's end.
target_learners: All families in the school community, elementary through high school
target_learning_goals: Academic success goals, behavioral goals, and a welcoming school climate
examples: The Ohio NNPS schools used this planning structure to organize partnership activities aimed at improving student engagement, which was associated with increased average daily attendance.
key_sources: Attendance — National Network of Partnership Schools (NNPS). (2001). https://evidenceforessa.org/program/national-network-of-partnership-schools-nnps/

article_title: Health and Socioeconomic Factors in School Readiness and Achievement Among Children Born Very Preterm.
citation: Haider S, Tsanas A, Batty GD, Reynolds RM, Roffe M, Whalley HC, Marioni RE, Richardson H, Battersby C, Boardman JP. (2026). Health and Socioeconomic Factors in School Readiness and Achievement Among Children Born Very Preterm. JAMA Network Open. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.23068
title: Novel linkage of the National Neonatal Research Database and National Pupil Database
description: The study created what the authors describe as "a novel linkage between the NNRD and the NPD" — the first, to their knowledge, "to combine these national resources." The National Neonatal Research Database contains data on all UK neonatal admissions from 2007 onward, while the National Pupil Database is an administrative dataset of educational outcomes for all state-funded pupils in England maintained by the Department for Education. This linkage enabled integration of maternal and neonatal clinical data with statutory educational outcomes at school entry for population-level surveillance.
requirements: Sufficient personal identifiers (NHS numbers) for record linkage; 27.7% of eligible children could not be linked due to missing or incomplete NHS numbers
constraints: The NPD does not capture children outside the state-funded education system, so home-schooled, privately schooled, or migrated children could not be characterized
target_learners: Children born very preterm in England
target_learning_goals: Population-level monitoring of educational outcomes after preterm birth
examples: The linkage supported a cohort of 15,857 children with linked neonatal and education records

article_title: From knowledge to judgment: A three-year longitudinal analysis of artificial intelligence large language model performance on the Chinese national nurse licensing examination.
citation: Zhan Xinju, Yu Weihua, Cai Jianshu, Chen Jionghuang. (2026). From knowledge to judgment: A three-year longitudinal analysis of artificial intelligence large language model performance on the Chinese national nurse licensing examination. PLoS One. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0353059
title: Validated 9,800-question NNLE evaluation corpus (2022–2025)
description: The study curated a corpus of 9,800 multiple-choice questions from NNLE examinations administered July 2022 to June 2025, drawn from officially endorsed preparatory materials, examination guides, and practice question banks. Three independent nursing education experts validated each question, achieving inter-rater reliability of κ = 0.89. The corpus spans six content domains per official NNLE specifications, with 2,200 questions from 2022, 2,400 from 2023, 2,600 from 2024, and 2,600 from 2025.
requirements: Questions in standardized Chinese text format with complete stems and four response options; exclusion of visual-element items and disputed answers
constraints: Questions requiring interpretation of visual elements were excluded; residual data leakage cannot be eliminated completely
examples: Used to evaluate 15 LLMs under standardized zero-shot prompting with temperature = 0.0
